description: Graduate-level study of the algorithms and impossibility results behind replicated, fault-tolerant systems: time, consensus, consistency, distributed transactions, CRDTs, failure detection and resilience engineering. Students step through protocols, inject failures into simulated networks and clusters, and finish with a replicated store project.
modelledOn: Attiya and Welch, Distributed Computing: Fundamentals, Simulations and Advanced Topics
Research papers on Paxos, Raft, Dynamo, Spanner and CRDTs
outcomes: Prove or refute safety and liveness properties of a distributed protocol under a stated failure and timing model.
Derive and apply the FLP, CAP and quorum-intersection results to decide what a design can and cannot guarantee.
Implement and trace single-decree Paxos and Raft, including leader change and log repair.
Compare consistency models and transaction protocols and choose one for a given workload and failure profile.
Design convergent replicated data types and gossip-based membership with analysed convergence.
Evaluate a production-scale fault tolerance design by reading a systems paper and an incident report critically.

units.title: System models, time and ordering
topics: System models: asynchronous, partially synchronous and synchronous; crash, omission and Byzantine faults
Physical clocks: drift, NTP, Cristian's algorithm and averaging-based clock synchronisation, bounded-uncertainty clocks
Logical time: Lamport clocks, vector clocks, version vectors and hybrid logical clocks
Consistent cuts and global snapshots: the Chandy-Lamport algorithm and stable property detection
Impossibility results: Two Generals, FLP, the CAP theorem and PACELC

units.title: Consensus
topics: The consensus problem: agreement, validity and termination; equivalence with atomic broadcast
Single-decree Paxos with its safety proof, and Multi-Paxos
Raft: leader election, log replication, safety argument, membership change and log compaction
Byzantine fault tolerance: the 3f+1 bound, PBFT and view change; blockchain-style consensus compared
Randomised and leaderless consensus: Ben-Or, EPaxos and wide-area latency of consensus

units.title: Replication and consistency models
topics: Primary-backup, state machine replication and chain replication
Consistency models: linearizability, sequential, causal and eventual consistency; session guarantees
Quorum systems: R+W>N, sloppy quorums, hinted handoff and read repair
Checking consistency: Jepsen-style testing, linearizability checkers and common anomalies
Multi-leader and geo-replication; conflict detection and the pitfalls of last-write-wins

units.title: Distributed transactions and commit
topics: ACID in a distributed setting: serialisability, snapshot isolation and write skew
Two-phase commit, its blocking problem, three-phase commit and Paxos Commit
Distributed concurrency control: two-phase locking, timestamp ordering, MVCC and externally consistent transactions
Sagas, compensating transactions, the outbox pattern and idempotency for mobile money transfers
Deterministic transaction execution, coordination avoidance and the CALM theorem

units.title: Key-value stores and CRDTs
topics: Partitioning: consistent hashing, virtual nodes and rendezvous hashing
Dynamo-style stores: gossip, vector clocks and Merkle-tree anti-entropy
LSM-tree storage engines, write-ahead logs and compaction in wide-column stores
State-based and operation-based CRDTs: G-counter, PN-counter, OR-set and sequence CRDTs
Convergence proofs with join-semilattices; offline-first applications

units.title: Failure detection and membership
topics: Heartbeat and phi-accrual failure detectors; completeness, accuracy and the Chandra-Toueg classes
Gossip protocols: SWIM membership, epidemic dissemination and convergence-rate analysis
Leader election, leases and fencing tokens; split-brain
Group membership, view synchrony and reconfiguration
Coordination services: ZooKeeper and etcd, locks, barriers and configuration

units.title: Fault tolerance in practice
topics: Planet-scale systems: a Spanner-style database, a Chubby-style lock service and a Borg-style cluster manager
Reading incident reports: storage and network partition outages, cascading and metastable failures
Resilience engineering: chaos experiments, circuit breakers, bulkheads, retries with backoff and jitter, load shedding
Performance at scale: tail latency, hedged requests, queueing and backpressure
Intermittent connectivity in Africa: delay-tolerant networking, edge computing and offline-first design

units.title: Verification, research and project
topics: Verifying protocols: TLA+ specifications, model checking and deterministic simulation testing
Critical reading of a recent distributed systems paper: claims, assumptions and evaluation gaps
Project: a replicated key-value store tested under injected partitions and crashes
Open problems: scalable Byzantine consensus, verified implementations and wide-area coordination

schedule.title: Failure models, clocks and logical time
schedule.exercise: Show with a message-sequence diagram why two processes cannot order events using only synchronised wall clocks with 5 ms skew, then fix it with vector clocks.

tasks.title: Assign Lamport timestamps to the events of a three-process message diagram and list pairs that are concurrent versus ordered.
Compute vector clocks for a five-event trace, detect two concurrent writes, and show which one a last-write-wins rule would silently lose.
Simulate NTP-style synchronisation across links with asymmetric delay and measure the residual clock error for each node.

schedule.title: Snapshots and impossibility results
schedule.exercise: Write out the FLP argument in your own words: what is assumed, what is shown and which assumption real systems relax.

tasks.title: Run the Chandy-Lamport snapshot on a four-process token-passing system and verify that the recorded global state conserves the total tokens.
Partition a three-node replicated service on a simulated network and record which requests a CP and an AP configuration each accept or reject.
Explore an asynchronous consensus execution step by step and construct the schedule in which a single crash prevents any decision, illustrating the FLP argument.

schedule.title: The consensus problem and Paxos
schedule.exercise: Prove that two different values cannot both be chosen in single-decree Paxos, using the quorum intersection argument.

tasks.title: Trace a failure-free single-decree Paxos round with three acceptors through prepare, promise, accept and accepted messages.
Run two competing proposers with message delays, show the dueling proposers livelock, and fix it with randomised backoff or a distinguished leader.
Implement single-decree Paxos with a message simulator that drops and reorders messages, and check agreement across 1000 random schedules.

schedule.title: Raft, Byzantine agreement and fast consensus
schedule.exercise: Compare Raft and PBFT in a table covering fault model, node count, message complexity per decision and recovery from a faulty leader.

tasks.title: Watch a five-node Raft cluster elect a leader, replicate three log entries, then crash the leader and observe the new election.
Create a network partition in a Raft cluster so a minority leader accepts writes, and show these entries are overwritten after healing.
Run PBFT with four replicas and one Byzantine primary sending conflicting pre-prepares, and trace the view change until a correct primary commits.

schedule.title: Replication strategies and consistency models
schedule.exercise: For each of five operations histories, decide whether it is linearizable, sequentially consistent, causally consistent or none, with a justification.

tasks.title: Decide for six read and write histories whether each is linearizable and give the linearization order or a counterexample.
Configure N=5 replicas with R and W values, inject two node failures, and tabulate which settings still give strong reads and writes.
Compare primary-backup with chain replication under a head crash and a tail crash, tracing which acknowledged writes survive each time.

schedule.title: Testing consistency and geo-replication
schedule.exercise: Design a Jepsen-style test for a replicated counter: operations, faults to inject, the invariant to check and how the checker decides.

tasks.title: Check a recorded history of 12 register operations with a linearizability checker and identify the operation that makes it fail.
Deploy a two-region multi-leader store, write the same key in both regions during a partition, and compare last-write-wins with merge resolution.
Write a nemesis that partitions and heals a simulated three-node store at random, run 200 operations, and report any stale reads found.

schedule.title: Transactions, commit protocols and sagas
schedule.exercise: Specify a mobile money transfer between two wallets on different shards as a two-phase commit and as a saga, comparing failure behaviour at each step.

tasks.title: Trace two-phase commit with three participants where one votes no, and list the log records written by coordinator and participants.
Crash the coordinator after all participants vote yes, show participants blocked holding locks, and explain how Paxos Commit removes that block.
Implement a transfer saga with compensations and idempotency keys, inject duplicate and lost messages, and verify no balance is double-debited.

schedule.title: Partitioning and Dynamo-style stores
schedule.exercise: Compute how many keys move when a node is added under modulo hashing versus consistent hashing with 100 virtual nodes, then explain the difference.

tasks.title: Place six nodes and twenty keys on a hash ring, add a seventh node, and count the keys that move.
Use Merkle trees to find the differing keys between two replicas of 16 items and count hashes compared against a full scan.
Build a small LSM store with a memtable, sorted runs and compaction, and measure read and write amplification for 10000 operations.

schedule.title: CRDTs and convergence
schedule.exercise: Prove that a G-counter merge by element-wise maximum is commutative, associative and idempotent, and explain why that guarantees convergence.

tasks.title: Apply increments on three replicas of a PN-counter, merge them in different orders, and confirm all replicas converge to the same value.
Implement an OR-set and show that an add concurrent with a remove of the same element keeps the element after merging.
Simulate three field-agent phones editing a shared harvest record offline over an intermittent network, then reconcile with CRDTs and report conflicts avoided.

schedule.title: Failure detectors, gossip and coordination
schedule.exercise: For a 1000-node cluster with 1 percent packet loss, estimate the false-positive rate of a fixed-timeout heartbeat detector and explain how phi-accrual and SWIM improve on it.

tasks.title: Configure heartbeat timeouts on a simulated 8-node cluster with variable delay and count false suspicions at three timeout values.
Simulate push gossip on 64 nodes, record rounds until all nodes know a rumour, and compare it with the log2 n prediction.
Build a lease-based lock with fencing tokens, pause the lock holder past its lease, and show the storage service rejecting the stale write.

schedule.title: Large-scale designs and incident analysis
schedule.exercise: Read a public post-mortem of a cloud storage outage and write a one-page analysis: trigger, propagation, why redundancy did not help and two design changes.

tasks.title: Add a circuit breaker and retries with exponential backoff and jitter in front of a failing service, and compare error rates before and after.
Replay a retry storm that overloads a recovering database, and apply load shedding and bulkheads to restore throughput.
Design a multi-zone deployment with a replicated lock service and cluster scheduler, inject a zone loss, and verify the survivor serves with no data loss.

schedule.title: Tail latency and low-connectivity environments
schedule.exercise: A page fans out to 100 backends, each slower than 100 ms one time in a hundred. Compute how often the page is slow and how hedged requests change this.

tasks.title: Simulate a fan-out of 50 backend calls with heavy-tailed latencies and plot the median and 99th percentile of the overall response.
Add hedged requests after the 95th percentile delay, measure the extra load and the reduction in 99th percentile latency.
Design a store-and-forward sync between rural clinics and a district server over a link that is up two hours a day, and test lost updates.

schedule.title: Verification, paper review and project
schedule.exercise: Present the project: the replication design, the invariants checked, the faults injected, and a critique of one weakness you could not close.

tasks.title: Model-check a two-process leader election with a state explorer and read the counterexample trace to the violated invariant.
Reproduce one claimed result from a systems paper in the simulator, and list the assumptions the authors made that your run depends on.
Deploy a three-replica key-value store, inject crashes and partitions through a failure-injection script, and prove no acknowledged write is lost over 500 operations.
